operations_plan.summary: Create a new, separate rounded-square cover on the +Z-facing outer surface of the central hub. Use the central hub's largest projected rounded-square perimeter as the cover outline and extrude it 0.254 cm (2.54 mm) outward from the existing outer face.

steps.description: Select the outermost +Z-facing planar surface of the central hub as the cover seating plane. Use face 53 of the upper rounded-square hub cap as the flush-contact reference. Confirm that its outward normal points toward +Z. Treat solid 2 only as reference geometry and do not modify or merge it.

Create a planar sketch coincident with face 53. Looking along the +Z face normal, project or convert the complete external silhouette of the central hub into the sketch. Select the largest closed rounded-square loop belonging to solid 2, including the straight sides and rounded corners of the upper hub base skirt; do not use the smaller inset cap/shoulder loop and do not include silhouettes from crossed-member solids 0 or 1. Constrain the projected profile to remain aligned and concentric with the central hub axis.

Extrude the closed rounded-square profile by exactly 0.254 cm, equivalent to 2.54 mm, in the outward +Z direction. Start the extrusion directly from the plane of face 53 so the new cover's inner planar face is coincident with and flush against the existing hub surface. Use a New Body/New Part result rather than Join, ensuring the cover remains a separate solid and does not alter solids 0, 1, or 2. Do not add holes, recesses, chamfers, or other unspecified features.

operations_plan.summary: Create the matching counterpart cover on the -Z-facing outer surface by mirroring the first cover across the hub center plane as a separate part, producing the same rounded-square outline and 2.54 mm outward thickness.

steps.description: Select the opposed outer planar faces 53 and 72 of the upper and lower hub caps. Create a construction midplane exactly halfway between these parallel faces. This plane represents the symmetry plane of the opposed central hub caps and will locate the counterpart cover on the opposite side without changing the hub.

Mirror the complete +Z cover body created in step 3 across the midplane from step 4. Configure the mirror to create a second independent body or component, not to fuse it to the original cover or central hub. The mirrored cover must retain the same complete rounded-square perimeter and the same 2.54 mm thickness. Its inner face must coincide with face 72, while its thickness extends outward toward -Z.

Verify that exactly two new cover solids exist in addition to original solids 0, 1, and 2. Confirm that both covers have uniform thickness 2.54 mm, matching rounded-square outer perimeters, and opposite outward extrusion directions. Confirm face-to-face coincidence between the +Z cover inner face and face 53 and between the -Z cover inner face and face 72. Check that the covers have not merged with, cut, or displaced the central hub, crossed members, pivot bores, connector, or transition features. Retain solid cover plates without adding unspecified attachment holes or reliefs.
